messages:
miguel: Heads-up — CobaltCorp NDA signed, want a Private/on‑prem POC. Main asks: preserve client src IP, mTLS to our connector, static egress IPs for allowlist, and SOC2 artefacts. Any immediate blockers?
ashok: Ok. Architecturally two main patterns: 1) PrivateLink + connector in customer VPC, or 2) on‑prem connector with a TLS tunnel to our private control plane. Both support mTLS. Sticky/static egress is trickier for transit setups.
sarah: For a Private deploy we can map sticky EIPs per-customer on our NAT pairs. On‑prem connectors do mTLS termination and can present either customer certs or our connector cert depending on trust model.
eli: Quick bandwidth estimate for POC — they said 100 req/s avg, ~3KB payload => ~25MB/min ~36GB/day? wait that's off, rechecking: 100 req/s * 3KB = 300KB/s ~25.9MB/min ~1.55GB/hour ~37GB/day. Peak burst could hit 150MB/s for short windows. Call it ~40GB/day POC baseline.
miguel: Good catch on the math, thanks. Sales needs a one‑page checklist for customer ops (firewall + DNS + certs). Can we give a firewall snippet to hand them?
ashok: Yep, here's a minimal allowlist they can paste to their perimeter team — note these are example egress endpoints for the POC (we'll provide final /24s):
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood POC endpoints
OUTBOUND to 203.0.113.40/32 tcp 443 # connector endpoint (control plane)
OUTBOUND to 198.51.100.22/32 tcp 443 # inference egress (sticky IP)
OUTBOUND to 198.51.100.23/32 tcp 443 # fallback region
# If using PrivateLink: allow interface endpoint DNS and AWS control-plane endpoints as needed
```
sarah: Add note: if customer does TLS‑inspecting proxy, they must enable TLS passthrough for our connector domains or host the proxy with SNI passthrough. Otherwise mTLS will fail.
eli: For certs: customers can bring their own client certs (we validate client CA). For Private deploy we support storing connector keys in customer KMS/HSM; for hosted connectors keys live in our HSM with audit logs. Put that in the security questionnaire answer.
miguel: Sales also asked about pricing: will a POC need a Dedicated reservation? They want burst guarantees for latency-sensitive traffic.
sarah: For predictable peak throughput we recommend a short-term Dedicated commit (monthly) for POC days. We can enable a burst pool at ~2x baseline for an incremental premium. If they'd rather not commit, we can run them on shared hosted with no SLA and potential preemption/queueing.
ashok: Action items: I will draft the runbook + firewall snippet + short SRA answer for the security questionnaire. Eli — can you validate bandwidth math and add a line about egress logging retention?
eli: On it. I'll also include a simple pcap-friendly sample for ops to validate connections.
miguel: Thanks — once we have the runbook I'll attach to the sales proposal. @sarah please sign off on pricing lines.
sarah: Signed off. Sending to AE now. :thumbsup:
